text.p: Here are the highlights of stories in the Danish press on Tuesday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

-- Denmark has won a battle in its fight against high-pressure postal sales methods by foreign firms that are forbidden for Danish companies. Dutch mail-order firm Bakker is not contesting a 10,000 crown fine by a Danish trade court.

--BG Bank's unsuccessful attempt to take control of the SDC savings banks' joint data network was part of a secret plan to merge with mortgage lender Nykredit and insurer Topdanmark, BG Bank documents reveal.
--Mobile phone charges are expected to fall sharply after the National Telecom Agency awards licences to three new operators to run a new and cheaper system.
-- Insurer Danica says it plans to invest at least two billion crowns in Danish shares over the coming year.
--The government plans to invest close to nine billion crowns to upgrade and modernise the railways.
--In the light of Den Danske Bank's takeover of Sweden's Ostgota Enskilda Bank, regional banks in Zealand are a target for Swedish buyers.
--Icopal was the end-buyer of Goldman Sachs' 6.7 percent stake in bid target Phoenix.
